# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg when the tag's GREEN push run already gates it, while
  # the release-specific legs (binaries attach, release-provenance,
  # installer-smoke) keep running on the twin (the retired comment here
  # only made the binaries UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create +
  # --clobber, last wins — while the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran,
  # doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays out — baselines are macOS-captured;
#                   the nightly build-release macOS row guards goldens on
#                   the pinned-font env, issue #1856 / #177 E5)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   office-addin-suite → Outlook add-in acceptance suite (gh-1659: moved
#               from the standalone office-addin.yml — its push/PR
#               triggers are retired, so a lib/**- or flutter_app/**-
#               touching PR gets ONE workflow entry; PATH-TRIGGERED on
#               pull_request + SM validation dispatches, same model as
#               exzone/locksmoke; the daily-publish addin leg still
#               dispatches office-addin.yml directly)
#   extension-size-gate → gh-1684 AC3: the fa-extension.zip size budget
#               gate at PR review time (was deploy-time-only in pages.yml,
#               which is how #1631 blocked Pages for days). PATH-TRIGGERED
#               on pull_request + SM validation dispatches; red blocks the
#               merge via the quality-gate platform class; the release leg
#               (build-macos.yml build-extension) keeps gating tags.
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never

#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
#   release-dedupe → gh-1625 release-twin short-circuit: the
#                `release: published` event fires a second run for every
#                pushed tag; when the tag's own GREEN push run already
#                gates it (conclusion == "success", recent window), every
#                gate leg skips (dedupe=true) and the release twin keeps
#                only its release-specific legs — binaries attach,
#                release-provenance signing, installer smoke (web-spa/
#                publish stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip
#                with it)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |

Now I have the complete picture:

The "Chrome boot tests" step:
- 14:35:08 — pub get done, warnings printed.
- 14:35:26–14:35:41 — quickjs native build + shader warnings (normal).
- 14:36:16.7735640Z — an empty-ish line (probably the `flutter test` compilation progress starting; flutter test output is quiet during compilation).

content.text:
# Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # gh-2072 (review thread 6): this job had NO pub get at all — the
      # prewarm below reads .dart_tool/package_config.json and hard-failed
      # on every fresh checkout, i.e. every v* tag run would red this leg
      # (and publish waits on it). Every other root-package leg already
      # carries the explicit pub get; this was the exception.

Whatever — that one was superseded by a newer dispatch and marked cancelled; the replacement run passed. Fine.

content.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user

# pr-2137 rework — CI red: office-addin-suite cancelled (degraded runner hang)

## Issues/Notes

- **Open review threads: 0** — `pr_discussions_raw.json` reports `threads: []` (GraphQL census `graphqlUnresolved: 0`). The single 🪶 NIT thread (bench-sim junk numerics) was already resolved and replied to in commits `16f4addc22` + `29d575296c`. `outputs/review_replies.json` therefore carries an empty reply list — nothing to reply to.
- **Owned CI violations: 0** — `ci_violations.json` reports `owned: 0, foreign: 0, unknown: 1`. The single `unknown` row is the generic `Process completed with exit code 1.` with no attributable file; judged from the raw log below.
- **CI root cause (from the raw log + Actions API, run `43237855777`, job `131251002777`)**: the Quality-gate aggregate failed with `office-addin = cancelled` — every other leg is `success`/`skipped`. The Office add-in suite job hit its **45-minute ceiling** (`timeout-minutes: 45`, ci.yml) while its step **«Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)»** hung with **zero log output for ~44 minutes** (step started `14:35:07Z`, last output line `14:36:16Z`, cancelled `15:19:06Z` with orphaned `frontend_server` + `chrome` processes at cleanup). A step that stalls silently until the job ceiling is the repo's documented **degraded-runner-allocation signature** (issue #194 watchdog doctrine in ci.yml: "a timed-out leg means a degraded runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run gets a fresh allocation… NEVER `gh run rerun`").
- **Evidence the hang is allocation flake, not this PR's code**:
  - The same PR content one commit earlier (`29d5752`, identical diff minus the main-merge) ran the same suite green in **5m41s** (13:34:26 → 13:40:07) the same day.
  - Sibling PR validation runs on the same mainline tree passed during the same window: `f76bf9b` 14:32:15 → 14:37:42 (5m27s), `044056f` 14:44:38 → 14:52:55 (8m17s), `6a999d1`/`cab4bcf`/`077a946` all 5–8 min.
  - This PR's diff touches **no file** under `flutter_app/` or `office_addin/` (the hung step's surface); the leg is armed only via the `^lib/` path-filter arm in the changes classifier.
  - All package-class legs (static, test-core ×4, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, faui ×3, CRAP, supply-chain, dep-audit, hostile-env, PTY set) are **green on this exact SHA**.
  - The in-run Watchdog could not self-heal this leg: it only watches `pull_request` events and its `needs:` list does not include `office-addin-suite`; this was an SM `workflow_dispatch` validation.
- A failed-jobs re-run attempt on the same run (check-run `131280432272`, started 15:19:12Z) cannot help: it re-reads `needs.office-addin-suite.result = cancelled` (cancelled jobs are not re-run by `re-run failed jobs`) and re-reddens the same verdict, and ci.yml doctrine forbids `gh run rerun` regardless (same degraded pool).

## Approach

1. Root-caused the red from `ci_failures_full.log` plus the Actions API (job steps, runner, log tail) — identified the hung «Chrome boot tests» step inside the office-addin-suite job, killed at the 45-minute job ceiling.
2. Verified with the Actions API that the identical PR content and sibling same-mainline validations pass the same suite in 5–8 minutes — ruling out a PR-caused regression; classified the red per ci.yml issue #194 doctrine (degraded runner allocation).
3. Ran the PR's full local verification set (7 test files, **339 tests — all green**) on this checkout to confirm the tree is sound.
4. Applied the repo's own sanctioned remedy for this failure class (the one the in-workflow watchdog would have applied had it covered this leg): **one empty-commit retrigger** (`ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)`) pushed to `ai/gh-2098`. The push fires the kicker → SM dispatches a fresh validation run on the new head with a **fresh runner allocation**; the office-addin-suite leg re-runs on it (healthy duration 5–8 min). No `gh run rerun`, per doctrine; the message matches the watchdog's loop-guard subject so the guard stays truthful ("one retrigger max per head commit").
5. No code change exists for this red: with `owned: 0` violations, 0 open threads and 0 conflicts, the Surgical Scope Guard forbids touching the reviewed PR code — and a review verdict of APPROVE with all non-blocking findings already fixed means the diff itself is done.
